:::{#rem-logarithm-formula}
#### The logarithm to base $b$ through the natural logarithm

For each $x > 0$, exactly one $y$ satisfies @def-logarithm,
namely $y = \frac{\logf{x}}{\logf{b}}$.
By @def-real-power, $b^y = \expf{y \cd \logf{b}}$.
By @thm-exp-log-inverse, $\expf{y \cd \logf{b}} = x$
holds exactly when $y \cd \logf{b} = \logf{x}$.
Since $b \ne 1$, $\logf{b} \ne 0$,
so we can divide by it.

:::
